hero.title: Authentic IELTS Full Mock Test Simulation
hero.subtitle: Test your stamina across Listening, Reading, Writing, and Speaking under realistic timed exam conditions. Experience official computer-delivered navigation, highlighters, and instant composite band prediction.

overview.summary: Taking a full-length IELTS simulation is the single most reliable predictor of your test-day performance. On test day, you sit the Listening, Reading, and Writing sections in a single continuous 2 hour and 40 minute session with zero breaks between sections. The Speaking test is conducted on the same day or within a few days before/after.

keyFeatures.title: Authentic Exam Flow
keyFeatures.desc: Strict timed progression through Listening (30m), Reading (60m), and Writing (60m) without pauses.

keyFeatures.title: Exact CD-IELTS UI
keyFeatures.desc: Split-screen reading passages, question navigation palette, word count trackers, and audio playback.

keyFeatures.title: Composite Band Prediction
keyFeatures.desc: Weighted algorithm aggregates your performance across all 4 components into an overall Band 0–9 score.

skillsTimeline.format: Section 1: Everyday conversation; Section 2: Monologue on general topic; Section 3: Academic discussion between up to 4 people; Section 4: University lecture monologue. Audio plays ONCE only.
Total length approx. 2,150–2,750 words. Texts taken from books, journals, magazines, and newspapers. No extra transfer time for answers.
Task 1 (150 words, 20 mins): Academic graph/chart description OR General letter. Task 2 (250 words, 40 mins): Discursive formal essay worth 67% of total Writing mark.
Part 1: Introduction (4–5m). Part 2: Cue Card monologue (3–4m). Part 3: Deep abstract discussion (4–5m). Tested separately or on same afternoon.

roundingRules.rule: Averages ending in .25 round UP to the nearest half band
roundingRules.example: Listening 6.5, Reading 6.5, Writing 6.0, Speaking 6.0 = 25.0 / 4 = 6.25 -> Overall Band 6.5

roundingRules.rule: Averages ending in .75 round UP to the next whole band
roundingRules.example: Listening 7.0, Reading 7.0, Writing 6.5, Speaking 6.5 = 27.0 / 4 = 6.75 -> Overall Band 7.0

roundingRules.rule: Averages ending in .125 round DOWN to the whole band
roundingRules.example: Listening 6.5, Reading 6.0, Writing 6.0, Speaking 6.0 = 24.5 / 4 = 6.125 -> Overall Band 6.0

roundingRules.rule: Averages ending in .625 round DOWN to the half band
roundingRules.example: Listening 7.0, Reading 6.5, Writing 6.5, Speaking 6.5 = 26.5 / 4 = 6.625 -> Overall Band 6.5

staminaTips.desc: Do not practice in 15-minute bursts. At least once a week, sit an unbroken full mock test at the exact time of day your real exam is scheduled.
Most test-takers experience mental fatigue 1 hour and 45 minutes into the test — right as Task 2 begins. Consider tackling Task 2 first while concentration is fresh.
Eye fatigue is real during 60 minutes of intensive computer reading. Practice scanning at 100% monitor zoom with good lighting.

faqs.question: Can I pause a full mock exam once started?
faqs.answer: In our training mode, you can pause if emergencies arise. However, for an authentic exam prediction, we strongly urge you to take the test in one continuous 160-minute session without pauses, mimicking official IELTS testing room conditions.

faqs.question: How are computer-delivered and paper-based IELTS tests different?
faqs.answer: Content, question types, scoring, and difficulty are 100% identical. The key differences: in Computer-delivered IELTS, you type your essays (with real-time word counts), hear audio through personal noise-isolating headphones, and receive results in 1 to 5 days instead of 13 days.

faqs.question: Do I need to take the Speaking module at the same time?
faqs.answer: You can take the Speaking module immediately after your Writing test or practice it independently. On official exam day, Speaking may take place on the same day or up to 7 days before/after.

faqs.question: How accurate is the platform's composite prediction?
faqs.answer: Our mock test scoring uses official Cambridge answer keys for Listening and Reading, combined with calibrated GPT-4o rubric evaluation for Writing and Whisper speech analysis for Speaking, achieving an average error variance below 0.25 band.
